x: The race for the minor positions was a different kettle of fish though,Barry Collins and Bob Holt just managing to get away from Mel Thorpe in the latter stages.
Hercules had moved up to finish 3rd, Bob Holt running 2nd fastest time. Our 'B' team gained the 'B' team awards after hovering between 12th and 8th positions, ending with the latter in 97:25secs.
Fastest of day: Gerry North 15:10, R.Holt(Herc)15:19, Luxford(Horsham)15:25, J.Bicourt 15:37, D.Holt(Herc)15:40, J.Snowden(Surrey)15:43 .

Belgrave looked set for second after good runs by Laurie O'Hara and Mel Thorpe, but Bob Holt(Herc) squeezed in front of Tony Fairclough on the penultimate leg and Chris Steer was passed by Collins (Windsor) on the last.
Fastest Times:- Geoff North and R.Holt (Hercules) 15:27

Once again the leading pack slowed up and Roberts (SLH) took the initiative with Bob Holt (Hercules) and Robinson (Achilles) close behind. With all this chopping and changing the inevitable happened and unhappily, Mick Gowan (HHH) was badly spiked and had to drop out.
With Bob Holt of Hercules also closing fast, only 11 seconds separated the first four at the finish. Blackheath were left trailing in their wake and were relegated to fifth.

Bob Holt of Hercules led Presland (Surrey) and Smallbone (Mitcham) at the half-distance with the Hercules and Mitcham teams pressing hard. There was virtually no change over the second lap, and with Belgrave well out of the running all that remained of interest was the handicap result.
Gerry set the pace throughout, but after the first of the three 2½ mile laps still had Robinson (Guildford) and R.Holt (Hercules) at his shoulder - the latter looking particularly relaxed.
… a very merry Gerry North dancing like a dervish in the centre and looking suspiciously as if he was trying to 'nobble' Bob Holt of Hercules (the County Champs were the next week-end).…

Assuming that all users of Arthur's cottage are paid up members of this second-claim "club" then there must have been some pride in achieving National placings of 4th (Hogan), 5th (Johnstone), 8th (R. Holt), 26th (Gowan), 32nd (D.

Gerry North was out for nothing more than a training run but, just to shake up the leading group during the race he put in a half-mile spurt to open up a lead of 100 yards and then eased up to await training companion Bob Holt of Hercules, whereupon they crossed the line together.
John finished one place ahead of Billings and 23 up on Ward. BOTTOM: A desperate North fights to hold off Bob Holt, Peter Welsh (Empire S'chase gold-medallist) and Mike Turner.
Laurie O'Hara had a shock on the penultimate leg when his minute lead was wiped out by new International Bob Holt who sped tp a new lap record, 13 seconds better than Gerry's existing mark.
BRIGHTON FRONT - Fastest Times:- R.Holt (Herc) 12:17, R.Gevers (SLH) 12:20, L.Presland (Sy) 12:21, A.Maxwell (W.Gn) 12:21, C.Moxom (W.Gn) 12:23, J.Cooke (Portsmouth) 12:24
Still more amazing, the fact that he was only 5th behind Tim Johnston (Ports/27:36.8), W.Olivier (S.Africa/27:41.8), and Bob and Dave Holt (Herc/28:05.0, 28:06.8).
The 3 mile final was John Thresher's first real test of the season and it resulted in a narrow defeat by Bob Holt (Hercules) with John stopping the watches at a p.best of 13:40.4.

How I bet John Thresher wished he had run in this one rather than the previous race for dragging along behind the Portsmouth star was arch-rival Bob Holt of Hercules AC who clipped John's time by just 1 second.
The 1500 metres was a pre-AAA Champs warm up for John Thresher and he absolutely romped away from a field including Hugh Pullan (SLH), two S.African Internationals and arch rival Bob Holt (Herc).
Fastest Laps: R.Holt (Herc)13.25, Gerry North 13.31, S.Badgery (Mit)13.34

He made it look easy and romped 7 seconds ahead of Bob Holt with John Baldwin (Blackheath) a further second away, third. Geoff North never really got going and probably hadn't recovered from his "good 'un" in the Bracknell race the previous week.

Inspiring our team out front was Gerry North, in great form, who took less than a lap to shake off Bob Holt, his main rival. Fairclough, Major & Bicourt gradually moved through the field and we soon had four in fifteen, so all depended on our last two scorers who were obviously better placed to gain points.

Once again Gerry North won the individual race, though this time having to share first place with the runner-up at Wimbledon, Bob Holt. Belgrave doubled their lead in the league table and go into the last race with a handy margin of 182 points - our highest ever.
Laurie O'Hara took us up to 3rd, Geoff North maintained it and Bill Dance passed the Reading man and held off Bob Holt to finish a worthy second and a moral 1st.

Trevor Hart followed on with his usual reliable run to take us to the front; Bill Dance held this with a slower time and then Geoff North had the galling experience of recording 3rd fastest time of the day, only to see his 8 seconds lead turned into a 6 seconds deficit by Bob Holt of Hercules/Wimbledon.
Manchester (Gregory) and Hercules/Wimbledon (R.Holt) had closed up to within 30 seconds. At this point our supporters felt more confident of receiving second place than at anytime.

Gibson goes with him followed by Bob Holt and a mud bespattered runner whose spectacles look more like sun-glasses. The crowd cheers, and the "blind" man surges forward as though suddenly equipped with an outboard motor, races past the surprised leaders in the straight and scores what looks to be a…
GERRY NORTH leads the ultimate winner Bob Holt (H/W) in the "Brockman" 10,000 m.
He managed to catch and pass Poly and Coventry but Bob Holt (Hercules/Wimbledon) and Wilde (Manchester and District) were in great form and both widened the gap considerably.

Normally, a 21 seconds deficit is something John would get his teeth into, but when it's Bob Holt ahead it's a different matter!. Inspired by the fine running of his team, Holt set out to settle the issue there and then, and smashed Tim Johnstone's course record in the process.
Although we all know the potential of Bob Holt on the road we also knew Geoff North to be running well as witnessed by his comfortable win in our own road race only one week earlier

Geoff secured sixth place in an excellent time of 44:55 just over 200 yards down on Bob Holt. Dick Piotrowski and Lionel Mann provided excellent backing in 15th and 19th places respectively, enabling us to take second place in the team race to the consistently strong Hercules Wimbledon outfit.
Although Gerry North was not expected to retain his title on this very fast course which favoured Bob Holt (H/W) he fought with great tenacity.

We have survived our bad patches because at all times we have had several runners fighting for that last place, and if Gerry North missed out through injury we would not be weakened to the same extent as Hercules Wimbledon's losing Bob Holt.
Bob Smith and John Bicourt lead the chase after Bob Holt (H/W) in the Surrey County 5,000m Championships at Motspur Park. Holt (14:14.6) won from Bob (14:23.6) with John taking the bronze in 14:39.8.

It was 2mins 19secs later that Bob Holt (Hercules-Wimbledon) set off in pursuit. Mother Nature decided to join in the battle at this point with a sharp burst of wind rain and cold which sent the officials scurrying for shelter.

We had a quartet at Parliament Hill attempting a fifth successive win in the Greater London Council championship, while Hercs.Wim had their brilliant trio of Bob and Dave Holt and Mike Beever wearing E.C.C.U. colours on the Continent.

Gerry North finished in sixth place in 40m. 12s., just under a minute behind the winner, Bob Holt of Hercules Wimbledon. Trevor Hart was just one place in front of Guy, who was followed by John Thresher, 18th, and a back-to-form Alan Black, 20th, with Tony Fairclough making up the scoring six.

… Shaftesbury from 16th to 10th with a time of 22m. 20s - cutting no less than 54s. of the lap record previously held by Bob Holt of Hercules Wimbledon (if the 23.12 by Medway's Dick Newble, who finished Bedford's stage in second place is left out of account).…

John was, however, brought into the 5,000m. as deputy for Bob Holt, of Hercules Wimbledon - only to finish an off-key 21st in 15m. 03s. Lionel Mann carried Beds and Hunts colours into 16th place in the 20-miles road race in 1hr. 47m. 17s.

Only when Bob Holt swept our local rivals away and out of sight on stage eight was it clear that we would be fighting it out for bronze. We won this secondary battle without difficulty, pushing the holders (TVH) into 4th place.

John Phelan ran a "blinder" and pointsmen were to be seen leaping up and down with excitement as he closed up to within 4 seconds of TVH and maintained our 3rd position as Aldershot sank back to 4th and Hercules Wimbledon rocketed from 6th to 1st with a 24:24 clocking from Bob Holt.

On Bill's shoulder was Bob Holt who managed to get by after the long hill had been climbed. Bill was also overtaken by Derby's Mike Tagg but still kept us in place by picking off the Hillingdon and Sale runners.

On stage 9 Bob Holt shook things up for Hercules Wimbledon who had at one point languished as low as 20th. He went up 5 places and in the process passed John Phelan but once again the Bels held their ground as Blackheath slipped behind.
Competing in a composite team: W.Laws 16:04; M.Manning 15:22. Fastest laps: R.Holt (HER) 13:28; R.Gevers (SLH) 13:59; W.Upcott (SLH) 14:04 ... 5th fastest J.Stow (BEL) 14:06.

'C' team: A.Mead (31) 20:58; P.Hardwick (30) 18:21; J.Stratton (30) 20:28; D.Davies (27) 20:16; J.V.Baker (26) 21:49; B.Marmion (25) 21:11. Fastest laps: R.Holt (HER) 15:10; M.Connelly (WAL) 15:12; D.Faircloth (CRO) 15:21...... 9th fastest J.Stow (BEL) 15:40.
John Bicourt ran one of his fastest ever 5000 metres at Wimbledon Park on August 23rd in the Melbourne Trophy. He tore away from Bob Holt of Hercules Wimbledon over the final 200 to win in 14:35.3.
January 3rd 1970 at Milford Heath and no. 80, Bob Holt (Hercules Wimbledon), leads the Surrey Senior Cross Country Championships from no. 13, Gerry North (Belgrave).

… Bels to change their ‘A’ and ‘B’ formula disappeared as at that inaugural Lauriston Runners meeting it was proposed by Bob Holt of Hercules AC, now second-claim Lauriston as well, that pairings for the Paarlauf should be made from ‘A’ and ‘B’ competitors to mitigate the disparity in competition.…
